subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Wing Design: From Biplane to Swept Wing
description: A fast breakdown of Wing Design: From Biplane to Swept Wing for builders.

hook.text: Early planes had two wings stacked on top of each other. Modern jets have one swept-back wing. Why the change?

buildup.text: Biplanes used wire bracing between wings for strength. The wires and struts created enormous drag at higher speeds.

discovery.text: Stronger aluminum alloys enabled cantilever wings — no external bracing needed. One thick wing replaced two thin ones.

twist.text: German researchers discovered that sweeping wings back delayed shockwave formation. This allowed flight near the speed of sound.

climax.text: The Boeing 707 used a 35-degree swept wing. It became the template for every jet airliner that followed.

punchline.text: From two wings with wires to one swept wing. Speed demanded simplicity.

quiz.question: What advantage did swept-back wings provide for high-speed flight?
options: Swept wings generated more lift at low speeds during takeoff and landing
Sweeping wings back delayed shockwave formation near the speed of sound
The swept design made aircraft more stable in turbulent weather conditions
